input: Assess the credit and counterparty risk of Beyond Meat

ownership.value: Public company (NASDAQ: BYND); founder Ethan Brown remains President & CEO; no controlling sponsor; shareholder base massively diluted by the October 2025 debt-for-equity exchange (Q3 weighted shares rose from 2.56M to 19.15M year-over-year) followed by a 1-for-30 reverse stock split effective August 13, 2026

financials.metric: Loss from operations (operating margin -144.1%, incl. $57.1M impairments and $20.8M Campus HQ charges)
Cash and cash equivalents including restricted cash

Cash and cash equivalents including restricted cash

financials.stated_by: Seeking Alpha / Distressed Value Investing analysis

debt_events.summary: Company engaged with a group of bondholders to initiate discussions on a balance-sheet restructuring (per WSJ, cited by Food Dive)

Raised/committed $100 million via a Delayed Draw Term Loan Facility; FY2025 financing activities included $100.0M of aggregate draws from the Delayed Draw Term Loan Facility with Unprocessed Foods, LLC

Exchange Offer completed: 0% Convertible Senior Notes due 2027 exchanged into new 7.00% Convertible Senior Secured Second Lien PIK Toggle Notes due 2030; produced a $548.7M non-cash gain on debt restructuring; shares fell more than 48% to $1.03 on 2025-10-13 after creditors accepted the dilutive swap

8-K disclosed private discussions with holders of the 2030 Notes on an indenture amendment to remove restrictions on repurchasing/exchanging the 2027 Notes for cash and/or equity and extend the make-whole period; company stated no assurance consents would be obtained

Second Supplemental Indenture with Wilmington Trust (trustee/collateral agent) amending the 2030 Notes indenture: removed restrictions on repurchasing/exchanging the 2027 Notes for cash and/or equity and extended the make-whole period end date from 2028-10-15 to 2029-01-15

Debt-for-equity exchange: exchanged $15.0M principal of the 2027 Notes at 96% of face value for ~1.55M common shares, leaving $14.5M of 2027 Notes outstanding (maturing 2027-03-15) — repaying debt below par with equity rather than cash

Court reduced the Sonate judgment against Beyond Meat by approximately $23.5 million; combined with the note exchange this reduced future outflows by nearly $40 million (existence of a court judgment against the company)

Filed Form 12b-25 (NT 10-Q): unable to file the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q on time without unreasonable effort or expense; expects to file no later than 2026-11-10 but 'cannot provide assurance regarding the definitive filing date'

credit_ratings.summary: No credit rating found: the FY2025 Form 10-K (filed 2026-04-09), the Q4/FY2025 and Q3 2026 earnings releases and press coverage disclose no S&P, Moody's or Fitch rating or outlook — the company appears effectively unrated, so no agency rating change in the last 12 months could be verified. (An Argus equity-research downgrade appeared in search results but is a stock rating, not a credit rating.)

missing_fields: S&P / Moody's / Fitch credit rating and outlook — none disclosed in filings or found in press; company appears effectively unrated, so no 12-month agency rating change verifiable
Company-stated cash runway / revolver availability — no figure in the Q3 2026 release; only an analyst estimate (unrestricted cash exhausted ~Q1 2028)
output.risk_rationale: Beyond Meat presents a high credit and counterparty risk. Revenues are shrinking (FY2025 net revenues down 15.6% to $275.5M; Q3 2026 down 8.1% to $64.5M) against enormous losses (FY2025 loss from operations $332.7M and Adjusted EBITDA loss $178.4M; Q3 2026 operating loss $93.0M including fresh impairments), leaving $169.3M of cash against $313.9M of debt at 2026-09-26 and an analyst-estimated exhaustion of unrestricted cash around Q1 2028 with $14.5M of 2027 notes maturing 2027-03-15. The company has already resorted to distressed-style liability management — the October 2025 exchange of 2027 convertibles into second-lien 7.00% PIK toggle notes due 2030 (shares fell 48% on the dilution), indenture amendments negotiated with creditors in July-August 2026, and a September 2026 exchange of $15.0M of notes at 96% of face for equity — while paying suppliers up to 19 days beyond term per Creditsafe and defending multiple judgments, including a court-granted attachment of ~$630,000 of assets in the Don Lee Farms case. Governance failures compound the risk: two material weaknesses with an adverse ICFR opinion from Deloitte, a late FY2025 10-K that cost the company Form S-3 eligibility, an NT 10-Q filed 2026-11-05 for Q3 2026 with no assured filing date, Nasdaq delisting risk after the stock fell below $1, and controller termination — none of it yet a formal bankruptcy, but the trajectory and self-funding capacity are those of a company in financial distress.

distress_signals.summary: Reduction in force of ~44 employees in North America (~6% of global workforce); appointed AlixPartners restructuring partner John Boken as interim Chief Transformation Officer ($215,000/month) and engaged AP Services core team at $135,000/week — hiring turnaround professionals signals distress

Q3 2025 results included $77.4M non-cash impairment charges on long-lived assets and gross profit nearly halved to $7.2M; material weakness in internal control over financial reporting (non-routine/complex transactions) identified per a 2025-11-12 SEC filing; Q3 earnings delayed ~1 week

Terminated corporate controller and principal accounting officer Yi (Jevy) Luo (last day 2025-12-23); CFO Lubi Kutua assumed principal accounting officer duties; Tony Kalajian appointed chief accounting officer effective 2026-01-12

FY2025: second material weakness (inventory provision accounting) identified; cessation of operational activities in China ($5.8M expenses); partial lease termination of El Segundo Campus HQ; $48.1M write-down of assets held for sale; $38.9M non-cash litigation accrual and arbitration with a former co-manufacturer ($8.1M legal fees); SKU rationalization/product discontinuations

Delayed Q4/FY2025 results and 10-K to complete review of inventory balances/provisions; company will be an untimely filer and loses Form S-3 eligibility (closing the ATM equity pathway); separate disclosure of errors in previously issued interim 2025 financial statements
Nasdaq minimum bid-price deficiency after shares traded below $1 since the start of 2026; continued-listing/delisting risk disclosed; 1-for-30 reverse stock split effective 2026-08-13 to address it

FY2025 10-K filed late: Deloitte & Touche LLP issued an unqualified opinion on the financial statements (no going-concern language) but an adverse opinion on internal control over financial reporting due to the material weaknesses

Rosen Law Firm filed a class action against Beyond Meat, CEO Ethan Brown and CFO Lubi Kutua alleging materially false or misleading statements about the book value of certain long-lived assets; working capital near multi-year lows, with bankruptcy and dilution risks flagged by analysts

Q3 2026 results included $57.1M non-cash impairments of long-lived assets and $20.8M Campus Headquarters charges; company repositioned as 'Beyond The Plant Protein Company' expanding into functional beverages amid persistent category-demand declines and revenue declines across channels

NT 10-Q / Form 12b-25 for the quarter ended 2026-09-26: additional time needed for financial close procedures and documentation of non-routine transactions, including an impairment of long-lived assets and certain lease modifications; no assurance on the definitive filing date

payment_behaviour.summary: Creditsafe data: 36% of Beyond Meat's 2024 bills were 91+ days late; 91+ day late payments rose from 9.7% (Oct 2023) to 42.3% (Nov 2023) and 69.7% (Dec 2023); company spokesperson called the figures 'highly inaccurate'

Creditsafe data: 'days beyond term' doubled year-over-year to 19 days as the company struggled to pay bills; roughly half of outstanding bills were 1-30 days past due in July 2025 (vs ~a third in Sept 2024)

L.A. County Superior Court granted Don Lee Farms the 'right to attach' nearly $630,000 of Beyond Meat's assets in a breach-of-contract case (sued under Savage River Inc. since May 2017); Don Lee Farms filed a third amended complaint naming Beyond Meat executives, alleging fraudulent alteration of a food-safety consultant's report; attachment protects the claim in case of bankruptcy
